premises.name: Filter.principal
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (s : Set α) : Filter α
premises.doc: The principal filter of `s` is the collection of all supersets of `s`.

premises.name: Filter.join
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (f : Filter (Filter α)) : Filter α
premises.doc: The join of a filter of filters is defined by the relation `s ∈ join f ↔ {t | s ∈ t} ∈ f`.

premises.name: Filter.sInf
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} (s : Set (Filter α)) : Filter α
premises.doc:
Infimum of a set of filters.
This definition is marked as irreducible
so that Lean doesn't try to unfold it when unifying expressions.

premises.name: Filter.comap
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (m : α → β) (f : Filter β) : Filter α
premises.doc:
The inverse map of a filter. A set `s` belongs to `Filter.comap m f` if either of the following
equivalent conditions hold.

1. There exists a set `t ∈ f` such that `m ⁻¹' t ⊆ s`. This is used as a definition.
2. The set `kernImage m s = {y | ∀ x, m x = y → x ∈ s}` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap'`.
3. The set `(m '' sᶜ)ᶜ` belongs to `f`, see `Filter.mem_comap_iff_compl` and
   `Filter.compl_mem_comap`.

premises.name: Filter.map

premises.doc: The forward map of a filter

premises.name: Filter.bind
premises.type: {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} (f : Filter α) (m : α → Filter β) : Filter β
premises.doc:
The monadic bind operation on filter is defined the usual way in terms of `map` and `join`.

Unfortunately, this `bind` does not result in the expected applicative. See `Filter.seq` for the
applicative instance.
